title: Carry the acquirer's loyalty data in field 63

blocks.text: The acquirer is launching a loyalty programme with a chain of fuel stations. Members earn and redeem points at the pump, and the data travels in field 63. The interface document's table for field 63 is copied into the comment at the top of `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Loyalty.java`. The link's packager is in the same file, waiting for field 63.
`purchase` already builds the request. The redemption step, which runs first, is written too. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `field63`: the declaration of field 63 for the link's packager;
`addMember`: the member's programme code and member number;
`pointsBalance`: the balance the host sends back.

blocks.text: When you're done, the host receives field 63 laid out as the document says, a member who redeems points sends both the redemption and the membership, and a response for a customer who isn't a member reads as no balance. About 14 lines in total, most of them XML.
The tests pack each message with your packager and unpack it again, as the host does.

cases.says: a member's purchase reaches the host with the programme code and member number in field 63
the points balance is read from the host's response
the member number goes on the wire behind its own two-digit length, not padded to a fixed width
adding the member's sub-fields keeps the sub-field another step already set in field 63
a response without field 63 gives no balance rather than an exception

origin.section: 6.3 Sub-fields Are a Nested Message That Only a Declaring Packager Can Carry

concepts: Setting a new nested ISOMsg replaces the whole field, while dotted paths add to it.
Sub-fields are a nested ISOMsg set by dotted paths, and only a packager that declares them can pack them.
